chunks: Ḥasan ibn ‘Abdillāh ibn Muḥammad ibn ‘Isā narrated to me from his father, from his grandfather, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Mughīrah, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Sinān, who said:

I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), “How should I say Salām to the people of the graves?” He replied: Yes, you say: “Salām upon the people of the dwellings from among the believers and the Muslims. You have preceded us and we shall join you, In-Shā`allāh.”
My father (may God have mercy on him) narrated to me from Ḥusain ibn Ḥasan ibn Abān, from Muḥammad ibn Ūramah, from Ibn Abī Najrān, from ‘Abdillāh ibn Sinān, who said:
He asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (peace be upon him), and he mentioned the like of it.

key_terms.أَهْلِ الدِّيَارِ: People of the dwellings (a common epithet for the deceased)

ai.seo_question: What is the correct Islamic formula for greeting the dead in their graves?
ai.summary: Recorded in Ibn Qulawayh’s *Kamil al-Ziyarat*, this hadith establishes the liturgical formula for greeting the deceased, emphasizing their status as 'pioneers' (farat) who have gone ahead of the living. The Imam’s instruction highlights the Shia theological view of the continuity of the believer's community across the barrier of death (barzakh), where the dead are not absent but actively part of the spiritual lineage awaiting the living to join them.
